RFC8955-3-1.note: Both halves now tagged both ways. Community half: TestRFC8955CommunityPolicyAcceptsAPermittedFlowSpecRoute (ipv4/flow and ipv4/flow-vpn with 65001:100 accepted) and TestRFC8955CommunityPolicyRejectsADeniedFlowSpecRoute (denied community first-match and implicit deny reject a FlowSpec route); revert records on evaluateCommunities. Prefix half: filter_prefix flowspec_test.go pair (accept, reject, missing, mixed), no record. Both at the plugin entry point: no .ci drives a FlowSpec UPDATE through a configured community filter in the running daemon. Rejudged 2026-10-17 (independent reader) after the owner-approved 6019dd0675 change to TestPrefixPolicyFiltersFlowSpecDestination: the filter input prefix changed from nlri to mp, the section keyword the filter text now uses for MP_REACH families. The cases are unchanged: ipv4/flow and ipv4/flow-vpn destinations inside 10.0.0.0/8 ge 16 le 24 must be accepted, and /25, out-of-range, invalid and mixed destinations rejected, with no unicast rewrite. A parser that stopped reading the mp form would fail the accept cases, and a policy that stopped applying would fail the reject cases. Package re-run green 2026-10-17. RFC 8955 Section 3: "Standard BGP policy mechanisms, such as UPDATE filtering by NLRI prefix as well as community matching, must apply to the Flow specification defined NLRI-type." The community units are unchanged. Verdict stands.

RFC8955-4-3.note: Re-judged 2026-10-21 (independent auditor, authored none of 4f0134cacd). RFC 8955 Section 4: "When advertising Flow Specifications, the Length of the Next-Hop Network Address MUST be set to 0." Row {partial}: tested "MUST be set to 0" (every FlowSpec advertisement with no redirect-to-IP-next-hop 0x0800 community); gap "Length of the Next-Hop Network Address" (a 0x0800 route leaves with the redirect address, owner-approved deviation for draft-simpson-idr-flowspec-redirect-02 Section 3, never counted conformant). Producers unchanged: internal/component/bgp/message/update_build_plugin.go::MPReachCarriesNextHop is the boundary on the origination rails and internal/component/bgp/reactor/peer_forward_facts.go::precomputeRedirectNextHop, with applyRedirectNextHop, on the forward rails. 4f0134cacd changed one line in each forward carrier: TestFlowSpecForwardingOmitsNextHop and TestFlowSpecForwardingKeepsLegacyNextHop now drive forwardViaRIB, the live forward (which keeps no FlowSpec rule since that commit) followed by reactorAPIAdapter.RelayStoredRoute per rule, the rail the rule actually leaves by. Assertions unchanged and exact: assertFlowForwardWire compares the whole MP_REACH value to AFI/SAFI/len 0/reserved/NLRI across unchanged, self, explicit4 and explicit6 modes with empty, peer-address and IPv6 received hops; the mixed test requires exactly two bodies, the FlowSpec one zero-hop and the legacy unicast one keeping its NEXT_HOP or withdrawn by its own gate, received bytes untouched. The forward revert records were already re-taken over the relay drive (unit-sha 516fac04981b0a39 in rfc/discrimination/rfc8955.json). Origination, route-server, wire-contract and flow-encode.ci carriers unchanged. Scope proven, whole requirement unmet; zero whole-requirement credit.

RFC8955-4.2-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-16 after the codec moved to internal/core/bgp/nlri/flowspec; units changed only by package qualification. RFC 8955 Section 4.2: "If present, it MUST precede any component of higher numeric type value." Positive re-parses an out-of-order build and pins the exact emitted order 1,3,5,12 (core writeComponentsSorted); negative feeds 5-then-3 and requires ErrFlowSpecTypeOrder from core parseComponents, with the same components ascending accepted, so the refusal is isolated to order.

RFC8955-4.2-3.note: Re-judged 2026-10-21 (independent auditor, authored none of 445b2e05f1 or 3bc47af4f2) after CheckMatchable gained the value checks in unmatchable_values.go. RFC 8955 Section 4.2: "A specific packet is considered to match the Flow Specification when it matches the intersection (AND) of all the components present in the Flow Specification." and "However, some combinations cannot match any packets (e.g., "ICMP Type AND Port" will never match any packets) and thus SHOULD NOT be propagated by BGP." The earlier weak finding is closed: checkPortValues now refuses port beside destination-port and source-port when port meets neither (Section 4.2.2.4: "This component matches if either the destination port OR the source port of an IP packet matches the value."); the reasoning is sound, since with each list non-empty a packet (d,s) exists exactly when port meets destination-port or source-port, and with one of the two absent the free port always satisfies port. Also new: one numeric list admitting no value its field holds (AND groups, values above port/ICMP/IPv4 packet-length/DSCP/flow-label/protocol widths), an IPv6 next-header admitting only RFC 8200 extension headers (RFC 8956 Section 3.3), contradictory TCP-flag terms, and a fragment list admitting none of the four packet states; the states match the Section 4.2.2.12 bit definitions (LF needs offset not 0, so FF AND LF and FF AND IsF admit nothing). Tests assert exact outcomes: TestCheckMatchable runs every row built, from the wire, as VPN and VPN from the wire with errors.Is equality, each refusal beside its nearest matchable control (port 80 / dst 443 / src 443 refused vs dst 80 or src 80 accepted vs src-port absent accepted; >1000 vs <=1000 with src 1000-or-1001 accepted; >100&<50 vs >100&<500 vs >100&<50-or-80; dscp 64 vs 63; next-header 44-or-43 vs 44-or-6; syn&!syn vs syn&!ack; FF&IsF vs FF-or-IsF); TestFlowSpecUnmatchableByValueRefused drives the config and update-text paths for the port, AND-group and TCP-flag classes; TestFlowSpecUnmatchableByValueReceivedRuleIsNotPropagated pins receive-side ineligibility, no install event and no candidate for the port, AND-group, DSCP, fragment and TCP-flag classes with eligible controls; the ICMP/protocol/fragment pair carriers and flowspec-unmatchable-refused.ci are unchanged in meaning. Polarity pairs are genuine and isolate the rule. Not judged a miss: lower bounds on packet-length against header sizes (the RFC names no such case, and its own "unable to locate the transport header" clause is implementation-dependent). Types-only callers (ExaBGP bridge, migration) pass nil matches and get the type checks only; the FlowSpec is judged again with values when built. The .ci revert record staled by the producer change was re-taken.

RFC8955-4.2.1.1-1.note: independent re-read: TestRFC8955FirstOperatorAndBitEncodedUnset drives config destination-port >8080&<8088 through buildFlowSpecComponents and the encoder, walks the emitted operator octets, and asserts the first carries 0x40 clear and the second 0x40 set; an encoder setting AND on the first octet fails it. The doc-comment edit in 6fac9359ff renamed the config parser only; the body is unchanged.

RFC8955-4.2.1.1-2.note: Independent rejudge 2026-10-21 after 74626ae4b4 changed TestRFC8955TextLeadingAndEncodedUnset. RFC 8955 Section 4.2.1.1: "In the first operator octet of a sequence, it MUST be encoded as unset and MUST be treated as always unset on decoding." Encode, guard: the positive now builds NewFlowTCPFlagsMatchComponent([{Value 0x02, And true}]) directly and requires FlowSpec.Bytes() == 03 09 80 02; core numericComponent.writeToAFI is the only step clearing it (`if i > 0 && m.And`), so reducing the guard to `m.And` emits 0xc0 and reddens the exact-byte assertion. Encode, real entry points: config (parseFlowBitmaskMatches) and update text (parseBitmaskComponentText) both call parseBitmaskTermsText with hasPrevious = len(matches) > 0, which refuses a leading '&'; the test asserts EncodeFlowSpecComponents refuses "&syn" (the operand is otherwise valid, so the refusal is isolated to the leading '&'), and the contrast "syn" "&ack" -> 05 09 00 02 c0 10 proves the encoder sets AND where allowed. No real producer can now hand writeToAFI a leading AND; the guard covers every other FlowMatch producer. Decode: TestRFC8955FirstOperatorAndBitTreatedUnsetOnDecode (unit unchanged) requires 05 05 41 50 81 16 to render identically to the clear form, [[=80],[=22]]. parseNumericComponent clears it at parse (`And: len(matches) > 0 && op&FlowOpAnd != 0`) and FormatNumericMatches guards again (`m.And && len(andGroup) > 0`); the test observes the behaviour through both, so a single-guard mutation stays green, but every other consumer (unmatchable.go expressionAdmits, unmatchable_values.go expressionWord, flowspec-firewall translate.go and numeric_ranges.go) is position-guarded or receives the parse-cleared value. Recorded break (writeToAFI panics) proves reach only; the guard-specific red is established by reading. Finding, comment only: the decode test quotes "SHOULD be encoded as unset", which is RFC 5575 wording; RFC 8955 says MUST.

RFC8955-4.2.1.1-3.note: Re-judged 2026-10-16: the unit moved verbatim to core compare_rfc8955_test.go, with only the family identifier renamed. RFC 8955 Section 4.2.1.1: "0: MUST be set to 0 on NLRI encoding and MUST be ignored during decoding". Wire op 0xf9 carries the reserved bit 0x08 and a leading AND. The positive requires the exact decoded []FlowMatch{{Op: FlowOpEqual, Value: 1<<56|7}}, so the reserved bit is ignored by core parseNumericComponent's 0x07 mask. The negative requires re-encoding to the exact op 0xb1, so reserved and leading AND are cleared by writeToAFI, and a missing end-of-list bit is refused.

RFC8955-4.2.1.2-1.note: Re-judged again 2026-10-16 after a comment-only edit. The new VALIDATES claim that parseNumericComponent masks 0x0C is TRUE: core types_numeric.go computes compOp = op & 0x03 for FlowTCPFlags and FlowFragment. RFC 8955 Section 4.2.1.2: "0 (all 0 bits): MUST be set to 0 on NLRI encoding and MUST be ignored during" decoding. Encode: assert.Zero(op&0x0C) over every emitted TCP-flags operator (MATCH, NOT, AND+END) goes red if the length, AND, END, NOT or MATCH bits move into 0x0C. The inputs carry no reserved bits, so deleting the 0x03 mask in core writeToAFI alone stays green. That mask is defence in depth: no reachable producer sets 0x0C, because parseBitmaskValue (text) and parseFlowTCPFlagMatches (config) build only NOT/MATCH, and parseNumericComponent masks received ops to 0x03. Decode: op 0x8D must render exactly like 0x81 (=syn) through the plugin JSON path, with the clean render pinned first. The decode proof is at the rendered match, not at the firewall lowering.

RFC8955-4.2.2.10-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-16: same units and same change as RFC8955-4.2.2.5-1. RFC 8955 Section 4.2.2.10: "Type 10 component values SHOULD be encoded as 1- or 2-octet quantities (numeric_op len=00 or len=01)." Packet-length emission requires exact one- and two-octet operands at 0/255/256/65535 across the typed, generic, config and text producers, plus recipient forwarding. Single-polarity as annotated, and the shortest width is local policy. Second re-judgement 2026-10-16: TestFlowSpecPreferredNumericEmission's typed packet-length producer is now the test helper packetLengthComponent (plugin types_test.go), which builds FlowMatch{Op: FlowOpEqual, Value: v} through NewFlowNumericComponent(FlowPacketLength, ...). That is byte-for-byte the matches that the deleted NewFlowPacketLengthComponent built at HEAD (plugin types_numeric.go:457-463). The deleted constructor had no non-test caller at HEAD, so no production producer lost coverage. The typed and generic cases now drive the same constructor, and the registered config, text and forwarding producers carry the distinct evidence.

RFC8955-4.2.2.11-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-16: the unit changed only in a comment path. RFC 8955 Section 4.2.2.11: "Type 11 component values MUST be encoded as single octet (numeric_op len=00)." Single-polarity positive: DSCP 46, 0 and 63 through the config producer each encode as exactly one octet. Core parseNumericComponent also refuses a DSCP valueLen other than 1 on receipt.

RFC8955-4.2.2.12-1.note: independent re-read: TestRFC8955FragmentBitmaskSingleOctet drives config fragment with all four flags through buildFlowSpecComponents (now parseFlowBitmaskMatches/parseBitmaskTermsText), walks the Type 12 operator list and asserts each of the four values is exactly one octet; a len=01 encoding fails it. Doc comment renamed to the shared bitmask parser on 2026-10-21; the body is unchanged.

RFC8955-4.2.2.12-2.note: Independent rejudge 2026-10-21 after 74626ae4b4 (unit change in TestRFC8955TextFragmentIPv4ReservedBitsCleared is the VALIDATES comment only; the parser it drives changed). RFC 8955 Section 4.2.2.12, of the four high bits of the fragment bitmask operand: "0: MUST be set to 0 on NLRI encoding and MUST be ignored during decoding". Encode: "fragment 242" and "fragment 255" go through EncodeFlowSpecComponents -> parseFragmentComponentText -> parseBitmaskTermsText -> parseBitmaskOperand, whose parseUint8 accepts 0..255 unmasked, and NewFlowFragmentMatchComponent stores the value, so 0xf2 and 0xff reach core writeToAFI, where `m.Value &= fragmentMask(afi)` (0x0f for IPv4) is the only clearing step. The exact 03 0c 80 02 and 03 0c 80 0f go red (0xf2, 0xff) if that step is removed, and 0x0f also tells the IPv4 mask from the IPv6 0x0e. Config shares parseBitmaskTermsText and writeToAFI. Decode: TestRFC8955FragmentReservedBitsIgnoredOnDecode (unit unchanged) requires 0xF2 to render exactly as 0x02, [[=is-fragment]]; parseNumericComponent masks the value at parse with fragmentMask and formatBitmaskValue also drops undefined bits, so the behaviour is proven at the JSON surface through both guards. TestFlowSpecFragmentReservedHighNibbleZero stays tagged but alone cannot fail (named low-nibble constants only); the row does not depend on it. Recorded break (fragmentMask panics) proves reach; the mask-specific red is established by reading.

RFC 8955 Section 4.2.2.6: "Type 6 component values SHOULD be encoded as 1- or 2-octet quantities (numeric_op len=00 or len=01)." RFC 8955 Section 4.2.2.8: "Type 8 component values SHOULD be encoded as single octet (numeric_op len=00)." RFC8955-4.2.2.9-1.note: Independent rejudge 2026-10-21 after 74626ae4b4 (unit change is the VALIDATES comment only; the producer grammar changed). RFC 8955 Section 4.2.2.9: "Type 9 component bitmasks MUST be encoded as 1- or 2-octet bitmask (bitmask_op len=00 or len=01)." TestRFC8955TCPFlagsBitmaskSingleOctet drives the config producer buildFlowSpecComponents with tcp-flags "syn&!=ack" and "cwr"; under the new grammar that is three terms (syn, AND !=ack, cwr), required exactly, and every emitted bitmask must be non-empty and at most 2 octets. Each operand comes from parseBitmaskOperand as a uint8 (names or parseUint8, 0..255), and writeToAFI takes its width from operandWidth, so a mutation widening tcp-flags to len=10 or len=11 reddens the <=2 assertion. The single-polarity argument still holds: no encode path builds a Type-9 operand above 0xFFFF (text and config are uint8; the decoder refuses valueLen > 2 for FlowTCPFlags, so re-encoding a received value yields at most 2 octets). Finding: the row's {single-polarity} annotation cites parseFlowTCPFlagMatches and config_builder.go:415-447, which 74626ae4b4 deleted; the producer is now parseFlowBitmaskMatches -> parseBitmaskTermsText -> parseBitmaskOperand (plugin_encode_text.go). The argument is true, its citation is stale. Recorded break (writeToAFI panics) proves reach only; the width-specific red is established by reading.

RFC8955-5.1-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-16: the unit moved verbatim to core compare_rfc8955_test.go, with only the family identifier renamed. RFC 8955 Section 5.1: "This ordering function is such that it does not depend on the arrival order of the Flow Specification via BGP and thus is consistent in the network." Compare is required to be antisymmetric and reflexive (a<b, b>a, a==a) over type, prefix, operator-byte and width pairs. Core Compare reads only component content (no peer, time or action). The arrival-order sort itself is exercised by RFC5575-5.1-1's TestRFC5575PrecedenceIndependentOfArrival, which this row does not tag.

RFC8955-5.1-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-16: the compare unit moved verbatim to core and the flowspec-firewall kernel unit is unchanged. RFC 8955 Section 5.1: "The relative order of two Flow Specifications is determined by comparing their respective components." TestFlowSpecPrecedenceFromWire pins, with forward and reverse signs and self equality, each of these: a lower type first, a present-versus-absent next component, a more-specific overlapping prefix first, a lower disjoint prefix first, equal-width memcmp, and received-width bytes over numeric value. TestSelectedFlowSpecKernelPacketSemantics adds Linux packet evidence that the more-specific terminal rule wins over a covering discard in either install order. That unit needs integration+linux privileges, and a skipped run is not runtime proof. The clause "If the common prefix is equal, the longest string is considered to have higher precedence" has no pair. It is unreachable for well-formed numeric or bitmask data: the end-of-list bit sits in the operator octet, so one valid component's data can never be a proper prefix of another's.

RFC8955-6-1.note: Independent semantic rejudgment: RFC8955 Section 6: "In the absence of explicit configuration, a Flow Specification NLRI MUST be validated such that it is considered feasible if and only if all of the conditions below are true: a) A destination prefix component is embedded in the Flow Specification. b) The originator of the Flow Specification matches the originator of the best-match unicast route for the destination prefix embedded in the Flow Specification (this is the unicast route with the longest possible prefix length covering the destination prefix embedded in the Flow Specification). c) There are no "more-specific" unicast routes, when compared with the flow destination prefix, that have been received from a different neighboring AS than the best-match unicast route, which has been determined in rule b." The existing receive-driven authorization units retain unique IDs, real received attributes and exact eligibility/candidate/selected-event effects. Tests separate longest-covering choice (with RFC9117 amendments), different-AFI/SAFI/RD routes, same-domain foreign-more-specific routes including a losing path, and removal-based reauthorization. Ignoring the losing foreign more-specific now incorrectly authorizes the route and fails the exact forbidden-candidate/install oracle; dropping route-domain comparison fails isolation while the valid matching-domain controls survive. This closes the specifically pending condition-c and route-domain producer counterfactuals without claiming that two faults exhaust all per-clause or dataplane behavior. The preserved broader assertions, not these two mutations alone, support the row. These are inspected scratch semantic executions, not canonical discrimination records. Current native record renewal/stamping remains parent-owned; no pending FRR carrier run, SRPM behavior, dataplane behavior, or full-RFC acceptance is inferred.

RFC8955-7.3-1.note: encode: config actions leave octets 2-6 zero and only 0x03 in the last octet; decode: every reserved bit set renders the same as clear for all four S/T combinations, and a pair differing only in S changes the render, so a renderer reading no bit fails; the .ci repeats it end to end to a plugin

RFC8955-7.3-2.note: RFC 8955 Section 7.3: "The use of the Terminal Action (bit 47) may result in more than one Flow Specification matching a particular traffic flow. All the Traffic Filtering Actions from these Flow Specifications shall be collected and applied." The same paragraph leaves interfering-action selection implementation-defined. TestSelectedFlowSpecKernelPacketSemantics now observes a received packet with the first rule's DSCP 10 AND exactly one increment of the later rule's sample counter; switching only the narrow rule to T-clear leaves the sample counter unchanged. Earlier controls prove T-set reaches a covering discard and that marking does not change the original DSCP used by later matching. rule_chains.go ruleChains/beforeMarkActions/markingTerms separate deferred marking and continuing action execution. Omitting the first action, the later action, or continuation fails independently, closing the earlier mark-plus-discard ambiguity. Requires a real privileged integration+linux execution; skips are not proof. Independent source rejudgment only; no test, mutation, build or gate was executed by this auditor. Native observed-red renewal is a separate parent step.

RFC8955-7.5-1.note: encode through config and EncodeRoute pins every reserved octet and the two reserved bits zero for DSCP 0, 46, 63, and refuses 64 and above; decode renders 0xEE as mark:46 and 0x40 as mark:0; the .ci carries the reserved-bit community to a plugin

RFC8955-8-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-16: the unit moved verbatim to core rfc8955_vpn_test.go, with only the family identifier renamed (test-local AFI 1/SAFI 134). RFC 8955 Section 8: "The NLRI format for this address family consists of a fixed-length Route Distinguisher field (8 octets) followed by the Flow Specification NLRI value (Section 4.2)." The positive decodes RD 100:100 from the 8 octets after the length and the destination component after them, and requires the exact wire back from WriteTo. The negative requires ErrFlowSpecTruncated from core ParseFlowSpecVPN for a length too short to hold the RD.

RFC8955-8-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-16: the unit moved verbatim to core, with only the family identifier renamed. RFC 8955 Section 8: "The NLRI length field shall include both the 8 octets of the Route Distinguisher as well as the subsequent Flow Specification NLRI value." The positive requires Len() and the WriteTo length octet to equal 8 plus the value length; its first assertion checks the fixture against itself, and the WriteTo assertion is the real check. The negative requires ErrFlowSpecTruncated for the same RD and value under a length that counts only the value.
